short_answer: Indian Cowboy is the selling name of Arun Shiva, a handicapper on the Doc's Sports roster. Doc's Sports is a Wisconsin pick service that says it has sold picks since 1971. On 20 Nov 2026 his profile listed football, college basketball, NBA, NHL, soccer and daily prop packages, and he had an 8 unit college football play posted for that day. In that sense he is a real, current seller.

Unlike many sellers, Doc's publishes pick by pick logs for several of his seasons, with the date, the pick, the final score, the units and the dollar result. We recounted five of those logs. The big headline numbers match: 84 and 54 for +$10,300 in the 2025 to 2026 college basketball season, 71 and 49 for +$5,820 in the 2026 WNBA season, and 15 and 11 for +$2,515 so far in the current NBA season. Two picks a forum member posted before games in September 2026 both appear in the log as losses, which is a good sign the logs keep losers.

What the logs do not settle: Doc's grades them itself at its own lines, the logs shown are the seasons the seller chooses to link, the football log on offer is from 2021, and some other claims on the same pages do not add up. Independent buyer talk is thin and mostly negative or neutral. Treat him as a seller with a published but self graded record, read the guarantee wording before paying, and log every pick yourself at the price you actually got.

guarantee: Longer packages promise more time, not money back. The football weekly package is "backed by our profit guarantee," and the monthly one says "you can use our self-extend service if we do not produce a profit." Weekly and monthly basketball packages say: "If the package finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program." Days when he releases no picks do not count toward an extension.

Day packages pay account credit. The college basketball day package says that "If the package does not produce at least $40 in profit across all plays, a $30 account credit will be applied the following morning," and adds that "College basketball daily packages offer next-day account credits only." The NBA day package says "Daily packages are eligible for account credit only; service extensions are not available." The NHL day package pays a $30 credit on a loss "(or profit less than $35)." The props package says "We guarantee you a daily profit with this package or you will receive a $30 credit." We found no cash refund terms on any Doc's page we opened, and the Doc's terms page returned an error. Your losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and with 4 to 8 unit plays they can be far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: Doc's Sports links a results page for each sport. Each lists every play in a date range with the pick, the final score, a W or L, the units and a dollar result at $100 a unit. We copied every row and added them up ourselves. Our totals match the totals printed at the top of each page, so the headline numbers are at least consistent with the rows behind them.

Our own counts from those logs: college basketball 2025 to 2026, 84 and 54 with 3 pushes, +$10,300, about 15% return on the money risked. WNBA 2026, 71 and 49 with 1 push, +$5,820, about 10%. NBA 2026 to 2027 through 17 Nov, 15 and 11, +$2,515. MLB 12 Aug to 28 Sep 2026, 33 and 14 with 1 push, +$8,700. Football 2021 to 2022, 76 and 60 with 2 pushes, +$4,755, about 8%. The return figure is our estimate, using the risk implied by each losing row.

Look at the split, not just the total. In college basketball, $6,640 of the $10,300 came in November 2025 alone. December through February added only $2,870, and the season ended with a losing April (minus $1,690). The worst slide inside that season was $4,100, about 41 units at $100 a unit. In the WNBA the worst slide was $3,240 and the first month lost money.

The windows are chosen by the seller. The MLB log starts on 12 Aug 2026, months after opening day, so it shows the part of the baseball season he chose to promote. The football log linked in his November 2026 posts on X shows the 2021 to 2022 season, not the current one. No NHL or soccer log loaded for us (both returned errors), so those headline numbers stay unchecked.

Other figures still disagree with each other. On the profile we read on 20 Nov 2026 the soccer season appears as +16,170, +16,600 and +17,200 in different boxes, and the NBA season shows as "+2000 YEAR" in one place and "+2500" in another. His X posts list last NBA season as "2026 NBA: +4376" and the year before as "2025 NBA: +2156", while the profile lists "2025: +4500" and "2024: 2500". His YouTube description says "over 15,000 Subscribers" and "Over 4 Million Views"; the channel itself showed 88K subscribers, so that text is simply out of date.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Indian Cowboy does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Indian Cowboy most often were IndianCowboyPix, 1218Sports, TheGodOfCappers, EZMSports. From 14 Sep 2026 to 19 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Indian Cowboy block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.

Result: 15 plays, 6 won, 9 lost, -3.96 units, a return of -26.4% per unit risked. By sport: NCAAF 2 won, 4 lost, -2.18 units; NFL 0 won, 3 lost, -3.00 units. By month: September 3 won, 4 lost, -1.42 units; October 2 won, 4 lost, -2.45 units; November 1 won, 1 lost, -0.09 units.

What it means: a 40% win rate on 15 decided plays has a 95% range of about 20% to 64%, and at the prices in this sample a bettor needed about 53% to break even. That range includes break even, so this sample cannot show whether they win or lose over time. The sample covers only the plays that others chose to post, which is not the full card a subscriber receives, and stakes are counted flat even where the seller rates plays differently.

What a buyer can verify independently: Doc's results pages are published by the seller and graded by the seller, at the lines Doc's records. We found no outside service that tracks every Indian Cowboy play with the line and the time it was released. We did one small independent spot check: on 24 Sep 2026 a TheRX member posted two of his plays before the games, a 4 unit Phoenix Mercury +10 and a 4 unit Phillies moneyline. Both appear in the Doc's logs for that date as 4 unit losses, at minus $440 and minus $520. Two picks prove little, but they are losers that the log did not hide.

What the seller publishes: season logs for the sports it chooses to link, season totals, streaks such as a "9-3 RUN", and a table of the previous day's results by handicapper. On the NHL expert page we read on 20 Nov 2026 his line in that table showed a 7 unit loss, minus $735. The logs show real losing stretches as well as winning ones.

What the numbers mean: a 59% to 61% hit rate at about -110 over a full season, as these logs show, would be a very good result if it held up and if a buyer could get the same lines. Doc's quotes a free $60 trial and says "91 out of 100 free trial accounts remain with us long term"; we could not check that. The NHL figures ("61%, +8,700" in one of two winning seasons in 2020 and 2021) and the 2013 to 2017 NBA figures have no log we could open.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Indian Cowboy is thin. We searched TheRX, Covers, Sportsbook Review, Reddit (our saved archive plus thread lookups), BBB and news. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found five independent places where bettors talk about Indian Cowboy, from 2024 to 2026, and none of them includes a tracked record from a buyer. The one buyer story is negative and secondhand: a 2024 Reddit post said a friend paid $395 for a week, lost money and was pitched a seven leg parlay as a lock. On TheRX, members in 2024 and 2025 asked whether he was any good or whether he handicaps baseball and got no real answer, and in September 2026 a member said they buy his plays and reposted two of them, both of which lost. One TheRX member in early 2026 complained that the Doc's network highlights hot runs and named other Doc's handicappers as the ones to fade; that post did not name him. On the positive side, everything comes from Doc's Sports, his own X and YouTube accounts, or a partner newsletter. The seller logs we recounted are favorable, but they are self graded. We found no billing complaints, no BBB complaint and no news or court record about him. Our Reddit search was partial: full text search of the archive timed out on 20 Nov 2026, so we relied on our saved copy of ten betting subreddits and direct thread lookups. There is no strong pattern either way.

In r/sportsbook, a user warned others away from Indian Cowboy, saying a friend paid $395 for a week of picks and lost money despite a guarantee, and that a seven leg parlay was pitched as a lock. This is secondhand and unverified. The $395 figure does not match the $99 weekly packages on his Doc's profile, so the friend may have bought a different product or bundle.

The 16 replies to that post were mostly jokes and general warnings against paying anyone for picks or trusting the word lock. One reply asked how he was still around and said people still fall for his picks, but gave no details. None described buying his picks firsthand.

Doc's Sports pages describe big seasons in college basketball, the NBA, the NHL, the WNBA and soccer, a doctorate in biostatistics and a large YouTube audience. Doc's sells his packages, so this is marketing, not independent evidence, although some of it is backed by the logs Doc's publishes.

The Rocketman Sports newsletter called him one of the most successful basketball bettors in the industry, quoted 2019 profits of close to +11,000, and offered a free trial from "our friends at Doc's Sports." It is promotion tied to the seller, not a buyer review.
TheRX daily service play threads list "Doc's Sports" among services members may not post. The thread gives no reason, so it is a forum rule, not a judgment on Indian Cowboy.

In a TheRX thread about the Doc's Sports service, a member said they track the network's handicappers the day after their plays, that the network highlights runs such as "7-2" and hides cold streaks, and that some Doc's handicappers are worth fading. The post named Doc's house plays and another handicapper, not Indian Cowboy, and gave no log. Another member in the same thread asked for feedback after using Doc's off and on for over 10 years. The claim that Doc's never keeps records more than one day does not fit the season logs we found for Indian Cowboy.

In a TheRX service play thread, one member reposted two Indian Cowboy plays, a 4 unit Phoenix Mercury +10 and a 4 unit Phillies moneyline. Another member replied that the plays always show up minutes after they buy them, which suggests a paying customer, and later said Doc's plays are not supposed to be posted there. Doc's own logs grade both plays as 4 unit losses that day.

In a long running TheRX thread, a member said they were looking at the Doc's website and asked for thoughts on several handicappers including Indian Cowboy. The reply, from a member who said they worked there for 20 years, praised a different handicapper and criticised another; it said nothing about Indian Cowboy.

A TheRX member opened a thread asking whether Indian Cowboy handicaps baseball. The only reply carried no text we could read. Doc's later published a 2026 MLB log for him, so the answer is yes for at least part of 2026.

His YouTube channel, joined 11 Dec 2013, showed 88K subscribers and 27,462 videos. The description calls him one of the most popular and successful handicappers in America and says he sells premium picks at Doc's Sports. A large audience shows reach, not results.
We found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about him, no BBB complaint, no app store page and no news, court or regulator record naming Arun Shiva or Indian Cowboy.

conflicts: Every record and season total is published by Doc's Sports, which sells his packages and grades his picks itself.
The logs shown are the ones the seller chooses to link. The MLB log starts in mid August, the football log is from 2021, and no NHL or soccer log loaded.

The Doc's FAQ says "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in," and the free pick on his profile says it is "Offered at: BookMaker" next to a "Free $60 Account Sign Up" link. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
The 2020 newsletter that praised him linked readers to a Doc's Sports trial, so it is not independent.
strengths: Pick by pick season logs are published for several sports, with scores, units and dollar results, and their totals match the headline claims we checked.
The logs include losing days and losing months, and two plays a forum member posted before the games appear in them as losses.
Prices and guarantee wording are published for every package, and there is a cheap one day option and a free starter account.
He posts free picks and long daily videos, so a buyer can watch his reasoning before paying.
A long history: a YouTube channel since 2013 and Doc's season figures going back to 2013.
concerns: All records are graded by the seller at its own lines. No outside tracker covers him.
The seller picks which seasons and windows to show; the football log offered in November 2026 is from 2021 and the MLB log starts in August.
Several claims on the same pages disagree: soccer totals, NBA season totals and the 60% versus 57% free pick figure.
Most of the 2025 to 2026 college basketball profit came in one month, and the season had a $4,100 slide.
The guarantee returns credit or free time, never cash, and his plays are often 4 to 8 units.
Doc's points readers to offshore sportsbooks, and the only buyer story we found is negative, though secondhand.
checklist: Open the full season log for the sport you plan to buy, not the season total. If a log will not load, ask for it before paying.
Check the month by month split. A season built on one hot month tells you less than steady months.
Count units, not wins. His plays are often 4 to 8 units, so one loss can wipe out several small wins.
Compare the line in the log with the line you can actually get when the pick arrives. A point or 20 cents of juice changes the result.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here it is credit or free time, and day packages need a minimum profit.
Start with a one day package or the free starter account before any season pass, and log every pick yourself.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper named Arun Shiva whose picks are sold on Doc's Sports at published prices, and Doc's publishes pick by pick logs for several of his seasons. Those logs are graded by the seller, not by an outside tracker, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of Indian Cowboy show?

We graded 15 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 14 Sep 2026 to 19 Nov 2026: 6 won, 9 lost, -3.96 units at one unit each. The 95% range of the win rate is about 20% to 64%, against about 53% needed to break even.
How much does Indian Cowboy cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 his Doc's Sports profile sold daily props for $25.00, one day packages for $30.00, weekly packages for $89.00 to $99.00, monthly packages from $279.00 to $325.00 and season packages from $495.00 to $850.00. The one year soccer package was $795.00.
Does Indian Cowboy have a verified record?

Not independently. Doc's posts full logs for some seasons, and our own count matched the headline numbers, such as 84 and 54 for +$10,300 in 2025 to 2026 college basketball. But Doc's grades those logs itself and chooses which ones to show.
What is the Indian Cowboy guarantee?

Day packages give a $30 account credit if the day loses, and college basketball day packages need at least $40 profit to avoid the credit. Weekly and monthly packages extend for free if they finish at a loss. We found no cash refund terms.
Does Indian Cowboy post free picks?

Yes. He posts a free play and long daily videos on YouTube, where the channel showed 88K subscribers on 20 Nov 2026, and Doc's runs his free picks on its site. The free pick record claims of 60% and 57% come from the seller and disagree with each other.

His posted logs show winning seasons in several sports at around 59% to 61%, which would be very good if a buyer could match the lines. What is unproven is whether those self graded results hold for buyers over hundreds of plays, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
